newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent products prices rise with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent products prices rise with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. midcontinent refined petroleum products prices, led by gasoline, rose sharply early Monday, but the rise was attributed solely to movement of futures on NYMEX, traders said.

Prices also received some upward push from differentials, especially on the distillate side of the barrel and in the Group Three region, but action was subdued enough in the early going to be dubbed dull by more than one trader.
Low sulphur diesel in the Group was heard offered 0.50 firmer at 6.25 cents over May NYMEX, but no deals at that firmer level could be immediately confirmed.
But a so-far wet spring in the nation's heartland was depressing agricultural demand, casting some doubt on the do-ability of higher diesel offers.
But diesel numbers in the Chicago market were indeed a touch weaker, with offers heard at about 3.25 cents over May futures, or about 0.25 cent weaker than diffs on Friday.
In any case, distillate markets were backwardated in both the Group Three and Chicago markets.
Gasoline prices were meanwhile steady in both markets, with prompt Group Three and Chicago offered at 0.25 cent under and 0.25 cent over respectively, traders said.
